body: My wife, our two grand kids and I visited Sri Devol Devalaya on 26th December 2019 after parking our car at the designated car park. Though this is a Buddhist temple, controlled by Buddhist priests, it is dedicated to "Devol", a local deity protecting fishermen and their boats. The entrance to the temple is by the main road. Visitors are required to remove their footwear at entry. The Devala premises is in two parts - on the mainland and on a small picturesque islet about 200 metres off in the sea.Passers-by and people who make offerings to the "Devol god" do so at the temple on the mainland temple. In addition to the main shrine room for “Devol” there are smaller shrine rooms for other popular deities, Katharagama, Vishnu, Natha and Pattini. At the mainland there are also a sculpted Buddha statue, an image house for Buddha as well as a bo-tree, fulfilling the basic requirements for a Buddhist temple.We also took a boat to the main shrine, perched on the rocky island of about 75 sqm. The disembarkation and re-embarkation at the island are risky as there is no landing jetty. Landing at the islet is on a somewhat slippery slab of stone. At the temple there is a specific place to carry out the “coconut breaking ritual”.People who visit "Devol" do so for a more sinister reason. This deity is said to be capable of placing curses. If a person feels that an injustice had been done, he may come here to seek divine justice seeking the god to curse that person. They do so by grinding chillies on a special stone on the island. This however is a double-edged sword. If the person is innocent, the curse returns to the person who originates it. Powerful god indeed!!We spent about 90 minutes at the temple including our trip to the islet of deity - "Devol".
title: Seek Divine Revenge for Injustice!

body: It is a nice little temple on a small island closer to land Seenigam Dewalaya in the Indian Ocean. It has an interesting story as it is said it is the only building that survived the tsunami in 2004, which is a Miracle. You get a very nice view, but if you really want to visit the temple itself, you need extra skills. The boatmen ask outrageous fares for a very short distance amounting to 500 to 1500 Rupees. If you are a very good swimmer, you can easily reach the temple by swimming. A very an old Buddhist temple situated on an island about 100 meters off the coast, and only reachable by boat. It is n very interesting location. It is lovely little Temple, mainly because of the settings. We went here not as tourist but as devotees; followed the procedure recommended for the believers. This experience inspired us. We spent about 15 minutes to go round in the tsunami photo museum. Do not take any intoxicants or meat as it is a holy place. It is the location where Seenigma Deviyo landed on his journey from India. The number of devoted local people far outweighs the meager few expat sightseers, making the temple feel more authentic and solemn. Well worth a visit and even if you don’t make the trip to the island, you can still take some scenic photos from the shoreline. The best time for the visit is 0700 to 1000 hours or in the evening after 1600 as the ground gets pretty hot. It is really worth a visit. It is very peaceful there.
title: Little Temple on a Island in the Indian Ocean Which Survived 2004 Tsunami,a Miracle.

body: Seenigama Temple or Seenigama Devalaya is a must visit place if you are travelling Hikkaduwa. Very easy to access . Close to Galle road situated on the coast of the sea, beyond the 96 km post on the Colombo Galle highway. Seenigama is a famous name among the Hikkaduwa Tourist Attractions. It is believed that the temple (devalaya) is 1300 years old . However the structural evidence states that the Seenigama Temple is above 300 years old. The sanctuary is also known as the Seenigama Devol Temple, owing to its patron deity, Devol. Devol ceremonies are prominent and often practiced along the coastal areas. Some also guarantee the success of fishing. The Temple is extremely sacred as it is believed that the deity resolves the problems of human beings. The land on which the Seenigama Temple is located in a small island can be access only by boat, You can see a deep freshwater well in the island.There is a annual festival at this place on August with two night perehera . An all-night pirith ceremony is held and it is followed by a Sanghika Dhana to the Maha Sangha.
title: Beautiful Small Island

body: If it were not for its history, we would not have noticed this temple. This is a usual-looking buddhist temple aligned to the main road north of Hikkaduwa. There's a lot of local crowd there, so doesn't appear quite touristy. Nevertheless, the atmosphere of this place is quite serene.The actual temple is on a little island few meters away from the land. We were not able to get there due to the rough sea and rain.Anyway, this place gathers importance due to the fact that this temple did not face any damage by the killer tsunami waves of 2004, even though the nearby villages were destroyed. Also, there are myths regarding this temple that one can avenge the wrong-doings of another person here, only if they've been victims to this wrong-doing. Interesting, eh?

body: Just to add over and above all that is written below the map location of this island is wrong. It is NOT adjacent to the coral reef area. It's a couple of km north. You can see it easily as you head north out of town and if you use the trip advisor map you can see the tiny island.It's also supported by a substantial roadside village selling bits and pieces targeted at the local market that appears to be linked to the temple. There may have been a festival just before we visited as the Buddhist flags and bunting was everywhere and there were a couple of elephants resting in one of the fields nearby too.If you were minded to make a day trip out of Hikkaduwa and not have to go far you could get the bus for R20 and see the temple, two Tsunami memorials and a Turtle sanctuary in one go.If you carry on north up the road afterwards for about 800m there is the Tsunami memorial (Standing Buddha) which is having a museum built behind it. In the grounds to the front there is one of the heavily buckled railway tracks. On the opposite side of the road to this and 50m further North is a turtle conservation and hatchery attraction R500 and very informative.Volunteers work therein the morning. And a further 500m north is the Tsunami exhibition with the photos and explanation of the plate tectonics. The pictures in the third room are a bit graphic for the feint hearted.
title: location on trip advisor is wrong, its 2k North
